title: Snubbed by Howard University girls at Murray's Casino
summary: Greer describes colour and class prejudice among Washington's Black elite and the humiliation of being refused dances.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Washington, D. C., all them pretty girls from all over the country used to go to Howard University, man, a guy We're dirt like me and you, we nothing. We're nothing. If you Wasn't a doctor or some of that crap, or if you wasn't real bad, you ain't got a chance. We'd be too dark for them.

At one time I went to a dance on Murray's Casino on 9th Street. I went there and got all sharp man. I was sharper than a tack then. Everytime you'd see me, I was sharp, and everybody they used to see me in the theatre, and carrying on. playing and showing off and singing. Noteriety, so I go to this dance up at 9th and R, Murray's Casino. I know I'm going

to catch one of those pretty -- so I go over I say, 'pardon me, miss, but may I have this dance.' She looked at me like I was dirt. Said, -- ain't said nothing to me. I went up to two or three more and they'd look at me like I'm dirt. Well, I feel embarrassed, so I swore, I say some day, I'll get even got-damned with these people. I thought they didn't learn to that crap down south or somewhere, but Washington, D. C. was terrible.
